Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨-y,\,x,\,0⟩$ and the boundary $S$ of a spherical solid of radius $1$ centered at the origin. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For a sphere or radius $r$ centered at $O,$ the unit normal to the sphere is given by

$$
n=\frac{⟨x,y,z⟩}{r}.
$$

In our case, we have $r=1.$ Therefore,

$$
n=⟨x,y,z⟩.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨-y,\,x,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =-xy+xy+0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}0\,\text{d}S \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
